description:
ABOUT ARCHITECT LABS

Architect Labs is advancing new frontiers in AI through silicon. Our goal is to compress end-to-end software to silicon timelines, and maximize intelligence per watt and per dollar for the world. Achieving this requires us to not only build our own radically competitive silicon products, but also reimagine how they are discovered, designed and produced at scale. We are a small exceptional team across silicon, systems, software and frontier AI. Our team has led research teams at nearly every frontier AI labs, and taped out some of the most complex SoCs in the world.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

When a part fails on the tester, how/what will we know about it? You’ll shape that answer long before tapeout. You’ll own the test architecture for all our silicons, make the case for the access and observability you need in RTL, and work with the test engineers who bring up the first parts.

 - Design the test architecture: Decide how to reach every core and memory from the chip pins. Define the scan hierarchy, compression, test clocks, and memory built-in self-test, then carry those choices through full-chip integration.

 - Make testability decisions in RTL: Work with RTL and physical design engineers on the hard trade-offs. A test point can recover coverage and cost timing on a critical path. You’ll measure both and decide with the block owner where it belongs.

 - Drive test signoff: Own ATPG and DFT signoff. Generate and simulate stuck-at and transition patterns, explain the faults left uncovered, and close on a pattern set that fits the tester memory, test time, and capture power budgets.

 - Bring up first silicon: Bring the patterns up with product and test engineering. When simulation passes and a part fails, use the fail log and scan diagnosis to narrow it to a pattern issue, a timing problem, or a silicon defect. Feed what you learn back into the next design.


WHAT WE'D LIKE TO SEE

Qualifications & Skills:

 - Tapeout experience: You’ve led and implemented DFT architecture, implementation and validation for  multiple blocks and full-chips or, including scan insertion,BIST, ATPG, and gate-level pattern simulation.

 - Fault analysis: You can trace a coverage gap back to RTL or constraints and explain which faults need a design change before signoff.

 - Tools and automation: You’ve used Tessent, TestMAX, or Modus on a chip program and written Tcl or Python to automate insertion, pattern generation, or coverage reporting.

Bonus:

 - First-silicon bring-up or volume failure diagnosis using tester data.

 - Memory repair or hierarchical DFT integration across a complex SoC.


WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive compensation, equity, and responsibility for the test strategy from the first RTL review through the return of silicon.
